scope_statement: 'The maximal globally hyperbolic development of generic asymptotically
flat vacuum initial data (4-dimensional Einstein vacuum equations, Lambda = 0) admits
no proper future extension whose metric is merely continuous (C0) and Lorentzian;
no differentiability, no curvature, and no equation requirement are assumed of the
extension. The class is about non-extendibility of the development; it makes no
statement about what an observer at I+ sees.
formal: 'forall r in D0: exists G_r subset X^r_vac(AF) with G_r comeager: forall
(Sigma,h,K) in G_r, letting (M,g) be the maximal globally hyperbolic development:
not exists a proper future C0 metric extension (M'',g'',iota) of (M,g).'

definition: 'A triple (M'', g'', iota) is a proper future C0 metric extension of
(M,g) iff: (a) iota: M -> M'' is an isometric embedding (iota_* g = g'' restricted
to iota(M)); (b) iota(M) is an open, proper subset of M''; (c) M'' is a SMOOTH
(C-infinity) connected 4-manifold, time-orientable, whose time orientation restricts
to that of M; the smooth structure is the category in which the metric is a tensor
field, while the metric itself is only continuous (worker-16 F2b-16-03 accepted:
a merely topological M'' cannot carry a classical Lorentzian tensor field); (d)
g'' is a continuous, nondegenerate Lorentzian metric on M'' (signature (-,+,+,+));
(e) NO equation is required of g'' on M''; (f) the extension adds points to the
future: int(M'' minus iota(M)) is non-empty AND there exist q in iota(M) and p
in int(M'' minus iota(M)) with p in I^+(q; g''), where I^+ is the chronological
future. The interior requirement blocks an extension that only adds boundary/dense-open
points (R2 major: clause (f) was escapable). CONVENTION CAVEAT: for merely continuous
metrics the causal structure can be degenerate and chronological futures may fail
to be open or may depend on the curve class (Grant et al., worker-supplied pointer
arXiv:1901.07996, UNVERIFIED); if the causal relation is degenerate, the witness
must instead be a timelike curve from iota(M) to a point of int(M'' minus iota(M)).
[R2 major, recorded not fully resolved]'
why_bare_metric: 'this is the strongest form of the statement: every extension class
with more structure or more requirements is a subset of this one, so ruling out
ALL continuous metric extensions is the hardest and most informative version.'
- extensions with locally square-integrable curvature (H2_loc) are a DIFFERENT class;
H2_loc is not C0
- extensions that solve Ric = 0 distributionally are a DIFFERENT, strictly weaker

- a 'continuous metric extension' is not required to make the geodesic equation
classically well posed; see the C0 uniqueness caveat
c0_uniqueness_caveat: for a merely continuous metric the classical geodesic equation
is not defined (Christoffel symbols involve first derivatives), so local uniqueness
of geodesics is not automatic and the elementary argument 'future geodesic completeness
of M blocks future extensions' CANNOT be imported from the C2 sibling. Non-vacuity
must be argued inside this class, not borrowed.
